Decision and scope

Range is optional and visible only for these exact stored divisions:

  • CP Fittings / Faucets
  • CP (QUAA / FERN)
  • PTMT & Plastic Fittings

No aliases, no dev-only PTMT, no combined divisions, no Pipes, Hardware or Ceramic. No Sink division exists; none was created. LAB-1 and LAB-2 remain Ceramic Sanitaryware / Lab Sink.

No catalogue/category cleanup, stored Range clearance, product movement, division rename/merge, Allied/ALLIED cleanup, Sales application change or live price write was performed.

Combined divisions are real stored values

The specific CP Fittings / Faucets | Ceramic Sanitaryware string is one stored division, holding 2 products in each environment. Products: RB-45, RB-46. Stored product creation timestamps are available in the exceptions CSV; they do not prove when the combined division was assigned. No field-assignment audit exists to establish that date.

The three combined values containing CP account for 7 products in each environment. There is also Ceramic Sanitaryware | PTMT & Plastic Fittings with 50, so all four combined values account for 57, not 7. All remain exactly stored.

CP | Ceramic is not recognized by the existing known Sales mapping; it is at risk of being dropped as an unmapped division. No mapping or product was changed. Sales handling is a separate decision.

There are 607 approved-scope products without Range in each environment: 334 CP and 273 PTMT. Range is therefore optional in all three divisions; no values were invented. QUAA/FERN currently has none missing, but uses the same optional rule.

The Single Product Editor keeps the current product’s Range read-only: vocabulary Add does not reclassify that product. Its price-source choice remains available to all products. Editing a pipe’s price preserves its hidden Range exactly.

Add Range retains admin-only access, division-scoped normalized duplicate refusal, typed name and reason, actor/timestamp and empty vocabulary-option creation. Division changes close and clear Add Range, clear creation-only Range input/confirmation, and invalidate previews. These are form drafts, not existing stored fields.

Part 3 — Master Category is a separate source

The authoritative loader now accepts Category only from the explicit category column in the products sheet. The source series column supplies Range only in the approved divisions. For existing outside-scope products, the upsert does not touch stored Range; for newly created outside-scope products, incoming Range is not stored.

A future genuine Category master needs a reviewed source and explicit trusted-source approval. The existing content-fingerprint/byte provenance restrictions have not been relaxed, and no fabricated categories were supplied to authorize a load.

Generic importer — premise clarified

The ordinary MRP-sheet parser did not have the stated RANGE-to-series mapping. It maps GROUP and legacy SERIES aliases to Category, and that existing behavior is unchanged; RANGE was not added as a Category fallback. The new-products workbook importer is the Range-aware path: Range is optional, recognized legacy column aliases remain accepted, and Range is stored only for the approved divisions. Outside-scope supplied Range is reported in preview warnings, not used to reject otherwise valid products. Existing hidden values are separately counted above and stay stored.
